definition_en: the process of judging the quality or value of something
core_image: 一份写满分数与评语的表格，被郑重地交到手上
scene: 学期末，学校会对每位老师进行一次正式评估。 At the end of the term, the school carries out a formal evaluation of each teacher.
sceneCN: 这里 evaluation 是「评估」（第 1 个义项：判断质量或价值的过程）；句意：学期末，学校会对每位老师进行一次正式评估。

senses.title: The judging process
senses.definition: the process of judging how good or useful something is
senses.definitionCN: 判断某事物有多好或多有用的过程
senses.example: The project is still under evaluation.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目仍在评估中。
senses.why: The noun names the action behind the verb evaluate.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 evaluate 背后的行为。

senses.title: A written judgment
senses.definition: a report that gives a judgment about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物作出判断的报告
senses.example: The evaluation praised her teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 评估报告称赞了她的教学。
senses.why: The result of evaluating is often written down as a report.
senses.whyCN: 评估的结果常常被写成报告。

intro.en: Evaluation adds -ion to evaluate, from French évaluer and value.
intro.cn: evaluation 在 evaluate 后加 -ion，源自法语 évaluer 与 value。

items.en: Valere means to be worth.
items.cn: valere 意为有价值。

items.en: Évaluer means to work out value.
items.cn: évaluer 意为算出价值。

items.en: Evaluate enters English as a verb.
items.cn: evaluate 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: Evaluation names the judging process.
items.cn: evaluation 指评估过程。

items.en: It also names the written report.
items.cn: 它也指书面报告。

note.en: Evaluation is the noun of evaluate, close to assessment and review.
note.cn: evaluation 是 evaluate 的名词，与评定、审查相近。

entries.definition: to judge value
judging value
someone who evaluates
a judgment about quality
a careful examination of something
a judgment of value or performance

normalIntro.en: An evaluation is the scorecard after the judging is done.
normalIntro.cn: evaluation 就是评判结束后留下的评分表。

normal.en: A formal evaluation follows official rules.
normal.cn: formal evaluation 按正式规则进行。

normal.en: Performance evaluation judges how well someone works.
normal.cn: performance evaluation 评判某人的工作表现。

normal.en: Carry out an evaluation means do the judging.
normal.cn: carry out an evaluation 意为开展评估。

normal.en: Evaluation criteria are the standards used.
normal.cn: evaluation criteria 是所采用的标准。

normal.en: Compare assessment: assessment is often broader, evaluation stresses value.
normal.cn: 对比 assessment：assessment 往往更宽泛，evaluation 强调价值。

abstract.en: Picture a form with boxes for scores and comments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有分数栏和评语栏的表格。

abstract.en: Imagine a seal pressed onto a finished report.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚印章盖在完成的报告上。

abstract.en: Think of a scale that has just come to rest.
abstract.cn: 想象天平刚刚静止下来。

examples.en: The new policy is under evaluation.
examples.cn: 新政策正在评估之中。

examples.en: We received a positive evaluation from the inspector.
examples.cn: 我们收到了检查员的正面评价。

examples.en: The evaluation of the course takes several weeks.
examples.cn: 对这门课的评估需要数周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evaluate（评估）＋ ion」——评估之后留下的那份判断，就是评估报告；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）→ 法语 value → evaluate（评估）＋ -ion → evaluation，核心义「衡量价值的过程与结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Evaluation first names the judging process, and then the written report that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: evaluation 先指评估过程，再指记录该过程的书面报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scorecard with marks and written comments.
core.cn: 核心意象：写有分数与评语的评分表。

branches.en: The process of judging is the first sense.
branches.cn: 判断的过程是首要义项。

branches.en: The written judgment is the second sense.
branches.cn: 书面判断是第二个义项。

branches.en: A report records what the process found.
branches.cn: 报告记录了过程所得。

branches.en: Criteria make evaluation fair and repeatable.
branches.cn: 标准让评估公平且可重复。

branches.en: A good evaluation explains its reasons.
branches.cn: 好的评估报告会说明理由。

intro.en: Evaluation adds the noun suffix -ion to evaluate.
intro.cn: evaluation 在 evaluate 后加名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, to be worth, is the root of the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere（有价值）是整个词族的根。

definition_zh: 厚；厚度；浓度； thick 一层
definition_en: the measure of how thick something is, or a layer of something
core_image: 卡尺咬住一块板：两面之间的距离变成了一个数字
scene: 湖心的冰层可以行车了，人们用卡尺量了又量。 The ice reached a safe thickness before the cars crossed.
sceneCN: 这里 thickness 是「厚度」（第 1 个义项：两面之间的量度）；句意：冰的厚度达到安全标准后车辆才通过。

derivatives.zh: 厚的；浓的（thickness 的形容词基础）
使变厚；变浓（thick 加动词后缀 -en）
厚厚地；浓密地（thick 加副词后缀 -ly）
黑暗（同用 -ness 后缀的平行词）

senses.title: The measure between two surfaces
senses.definition: the distance between two opposite surfaces of something solid
senses.definitionCN: 固体两个相对表面之间的距离
senses.example: The thickness of the door blocks most street noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇门的厚度挡住了街上大部分噪音。
senses.why: The adjective thick measures; adding -ness turns the measurement itself into a thing you can name and count.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 thick 负责测量；加上 -ness 后，测量结果本身变成可以命名与计数的名词。

senses.title: Density of a liquid or substance
senses.definition: the degree to which a liquid or soft substance does not flow easily
senses.definitionCN: 液体或软性物质不易流动的程度
senses.example: Cook the jam until it reaches the right thickness.
senses.exampleCN: 把果酱熬到合适的稠度。
senses.why: The same measure works inside matter: how much substance is crowded into the space decides the flow.
senses.whyCN: 同一种度量也作用于物质内部：挤进同一空间的物质多少决定了流动性。

senses.title: A layer of something spread
senses.definition: a layer of a substance lying on a surface, or a dense mass in the air
senses.definitionCN: 铺在表面上的物质层，或空气中浓密的一团
senses.example: A thickness of dust covered every shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 每层架子上都积了厚厚一层灰。
senses.why: Once you can measure thickness, the thing measured can also be lifted out and treated as an object in itself.
senses.whyCN: 厚度既然可以度量，被度量的那层东西也就能被单独拎出来当作一个对象。

senses.title: The middle of a solid mass
senses.definition: the middle or densest part of something, as in the thickness of a forest
senses.definitionCN: 某物最厚实或最密的部分，如密林深处
senses.example: They lost their way in the thickness of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在密林深处迷了路。
senses.why: The densest interior feels like the deep of the mass, where layers press from every side at once.
senses.whyCN: 最密的内部让人觉得像实体深处，各方的层叠同时挤压过来。

intro.en: Thickness is thick plus the old English noun ending -ness, one of the most durable suffixes in the language, turning any adjective into the name of its quality.
intro.cn: thickness 由 thick 加古英语名词后缀 -ness 构成；-ness 是英语最耐久的后缀之一，能把任何形容词变成其性质的名称。

items.en: The adjective root is the common Germanic word for thick and pressed close.
items.cn: 形容词词根是日耳曼语族共有的「厚、挤压紧密」一词。

items.en: Old English formed Thicnes(or thickness) with the suffix -nes, already meaning the quality of being thick.
items.cn: 古英语用后缀 -nes 构成 Thicnes(or thickness)，已表示「厚的性质」。

items.en: Middle English thiknesse served for layers, crowds and fluids alike, spreading with the crafts that measured cloth, metal and glass.
items.cn: 中古英语 thiknesse 兼指层、群与流体，随量布、量金属、量玻璃的手工业而推广。

items.en: Engineering made the word technical: wall thickness, plate thickness, coating thickness all became precise industrial terms.
items.cn: 工程学使该词技术化：壁厚、板厚、涂层厚度都成为精确的工业术语。

items.en: The figurative uses, the thickness of the crowd or of the silence, keep the physical image alive.
items.cn: 人群之密、沉默之浓等比喻用法让物理意象保持鲜活。

note.en: The first group holds the -ness family built on thick; the second gathers nouns of measure and depth.
note.cn: 第一组是基于 thick 的 -ness 词族；第二组是表量度与深度的名词。

entries.definition: the adjective that thickness names the quality of
entries.definitionCN: thick：thickness 所命名之性质的形容词

entries.definition: the verb of making thicker
the state of being ill; shares the -ness ending but not the root
entries.definitionCN: 疾病；同用 -ness 后缀但词根不同

entries.definition: the distance from top to bottom or front to back
entries.definitionCN: 深度；从前到后或从上到下的距离

entries.definition: the distance from side to side
entries.definitionCN: 宽度；从一侧到另一侧的距离

entries.definition: the degree of crowding of matter in a space
entries.definitionCN: 密度；物质在空间中的密集程度

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: thick plus -ness, the measure words of the same shape, and the layer sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：thick 加 -ness、同形量度词、以及「一层」的义项。

normal.en: Thickness = how thick: the adjective becomes a number.
normal.cn: thickness 就是「有多厚」：形容词变成了数字。

normal.en: Depth, width, length, thickness: the four measures of any solid.
normal.cn: 深、宽、长、厚：任何固体的四项量度。

normal.en: Jam is judged by its thickness, soup by its thinness.
normal.cn: 果酱看稠度，汤看稀薄度。

normal.en: A thickness of dust: the measure becomes a layer you can wipe away.
normal.cn: a thickness of dust：量度变成能擦掉的一层灰。

normal.en: The thickness of the forest is where paths give up.
normal.cn: 密林深处是小路认输的地方。

abstract.en: Thickness is the answer to the question every solid is asked.
abstract.cn: thickness 是每个固体都被问到的问题的答案。

abstract.en: A number that began as a feeling of pressure between two palms.
abstract.cn: 一个数字，最初是两只手掌之间的挤压感。

abstract.en: Every crowd has a thickness you could almost weigh.
abstract.cn: 每群人都有几乎可以称量的厚度。

examples.en: The thickness of the ice was checked twice.
examples.cn: 冰的厚度被检查了两遍。

examples.en: Adjust the thickness of the line in the settings.
examples.cn: 在设置里调整线条的粗细。

examples.en: A thickness of fog hid the whole valley.
examples.cn: 一团浓雾遮住了整个山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希克纳斯」——厚到希奇的纳斯卡地画，量量多厚 → thickness 厚度

root: thick「厚的」（日耳曼本土词根）+ -ness「性质」（古英语 -nes）→ 「厚的性质」即厚度；与 depth、width 同属本土量度名词系统。

sensesIntro.en: Thickness first names a measurement, then the density that causes it, the layer you can see, and the deep middle of a solid mass.
sensesIntro.cn: thickness 先指一个测量值，再指造成它的浓度、看得见的那一层，以及实体的深处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the gap between two faces, caught and turned into a number.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面之间的空隙被卡住，变成一个数字。

branches.en: The plain measurement of solid things.
branches.cn: 固体的朴素测量。

branches.en: How much substance crowds a liquid.
branches.cn: 液体里挤了多少物质。

branches.en: The layer you can point at and wipe away.
branches.cn: 可以指着并擦掉的那一层。

branches.en: The deepest part, where the mass is thickest.
branches.cn: 实体最厚实的深处。

branches.en: Both are the same number seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 两者是同一数字的内外两副面孔。

intro.en: Thickness is a textbook case of the suffix -ness: adjective in, quality noun out.
intro.cn: thickness 是后缀 -ness 的教科书案例：形容词进，性质名词出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source; -ness is a native English suffix, so the Latin entry list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语来源；-ness 为本土后缀，拉丁词条留空。

The warmth of the room eased him.

definition_en: coming after the fifty-ninth, or one of sixty equal parts
core_image: 领奖台上标着第六十名的牌子
scene: 这是她第六十次参加这项比赛。 This is her sixtieth time in this competition.
sceneCN: 这里 sixtieth 是「第六十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是她第六十次参加这项比赛。

senses.title: The ordinal after fifty-nine
senses.definition: coming after the fifty-ninth in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列中排在第五十九之后的
senses.example: This is her sixtieth time in this competition.
senses.exampleCN: 这是她第六十次参加这项比赛。
senses.why: Ordinal numbers mark a position in order.
senses.whyCN: 序数词标记在顺序中的位置。

senses.title: One part in sixty
senses.definition: one of sixty equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被分成六十等份中的一份
senses.example: One sixtieth of the budget went to travel.
senses.exampleCN: 预算的六十分之一用于差旅。
senses.why: The same form also names a fraction.
senses.whyCN: 同一形式也可以表示分数。

intro.en: Sixtieth is the ordinal built from sixty.
intro.cn: sixtieth 是由 sixty 构成的序数词。

items.en: Sixtig meant sixty.
items.cn: sixtig 意为六十。

items.en: The ordinal ending -tha marked order.
items.cn: 序数词尾 -tha 标记顺序。

items.en: The form became sixtithe.

items.en: The spelling settled as sixtieth.
items.cn: 拼写最终定型为 sixtieth。

items.en: It also names a fraction of sixty parts.

note.en: Sixtieth is compared with look-alike ordinals and nearby numbers.
note.cn: 把 sixtieth 与形近序数词以及相邻数字作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sixtieth marks the sixtieth step in a long count.
normalIntro.cn: sixtieth 标记漫长计数中的第六十步。

normal.en: This is her sixtieth time in this competition.

normal.en: The sixtieth day was the last of the course.

normal.en: They held a party for her sixtieth birthday.

normal.en: He finished in sixtieth place.

normal.en: One sixtieth of the budget went to travel.

abstract.en: The sixtieth step is still one step.

abstract.en: Small fractions add up to a whole.

abstract.en: Order gives a long journey a shape.

sensesIntro.en: Sixtieth is both the ordinal for sixty and the fraction one in sixty.

core.en: The sixtieth position, or one part in sixty.

branches.en: A long list reaches its sixtieth item.

branches.en: One part is measured out of sixty.

branches.en: A birthday marks sixty full years.

branches.en: Order and division share the number sixty.

branches.en: Tiny fractions still count in the whole.

intro.en: Sixtieth belongs to the number family of six.

latinIntro.en: The number words are Germanic, not Latin.

definition_en: a part of the sea partly surrounded by land, a marked space, or a deep bark
core_image: 被陆地环抱的一弯静水，泊着几只小船
scene: 船慢慢驶进避风的水面。 The boat anchored in the bay.
sceneCN: 这里 bay 是「海湾」（第 1 个义项：三面被陆地环抱的海水区域）；句意是船停泊在海湾里。

derivatives.zh: 由 bay 与 side 复合，义为「湾畔的」
由 bay 与 front 复合，义为「临湾的」

senses.title: A sheltered part of the sea
senses.definition: a part of the sea partly surrounded by land
senses.definitionCN: 部分被陆地包围的海水区域
senses.example: The boat anchored in the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 船停泊在海湾里。
senses.why: This sense came through Old French baie from Latin baia, a harbour.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项经古法语 baie 来自拉丁语 baia「港湾」。

senses.title: A marked space
senses.definition: a marked space for parking or loading
senses.definitionCN: 划出来用于停车或装卸的空间
senses.example: He parked in the loading bay.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车停在装卸区。
senses.why: The idea of a recess or opening in a building gave the modern parking sense.
senses.whyCN: 建筑中「凹进去的开口」这一概念，发展出今天的停车位义。

senses.title: A deep bark
senses.definition: to make a long deep bark
senses.definitionCN: 发出长而低沉的吠声
senses.example: The hounds bayed all night.
senses.exampleCN: 猎犬整夜吠叫。
senses.why: This sense came from a separate Old French verb abaiier, to bark.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个古法语动词 abaiier「吠叫」。

intro.en: Bay has two unrelated origins, one for water and one for barking.
intro.cn: bay 有两个互不相关的来源，一个指水域，一个指吠叫。

items.en: baie meant an opening or a bay.
items.cn: baie 意为「开口、海湾」。

items.en: baia named a harbour bay.
items.cn: baia 指港湾。

items.en: abaiier meant to bark.
items.cn: abaiier 意为「吠叫」。

items.en: bay covered both the water and the bark.

items.en: bay added the sense of a marked space.
items.cn: 现代英语中 bay 又指划出的隔间。

items.en: bay is common in coast, parking and hunting.

normal.en: The plural is bays.

normal.en: A parking bay is one marked space.

abstract.en: See a hound howling at the moon.
abstract.cn: 想象猎犬对着月亮长吠。

examples.en: The boat anchored in the bay.
examples.cn: 船停泊在海湾里。

examples.en: He parked in the loading bay.
examples.cn: 他把车停在装卸区。

examples.en: The hounds bayed all night.
examples.cn: 猎犬整夜吠叫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 bay 想成一道弯弯的海岸线，也可以是一个方方正正的车位。

root: 水域义源自拉丁语 baia「港湾」，经古法语 baie 进入英语；隔间义由「凹进去的空间」引申；吠叫义源自另一词古法语 abaiier「吠叫」。三义同形异源。

sensesIntro.en: A curve of sea, a marked space and a deep bark share one spelling.
sensesIntro.cn: 一弯海水、一块划出的空间与一声长吠，共用一个拼写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calm curve of water held by land.
core.cn: 核心意象：被陆地环抱的一弯静水。

branches.en: a sheltered bay
branches.cn: 避风的海湾

branches.en: across the bay
branches.cn: 隔着海湾

branches.en: a parking bay
branches.cn: 停车位

branches.en: a loading bay
branches.cn: 装卸区

branches.en: bay at the moon
branches.cn: 对月吠叫

intro.en: Bay forms few derived words; its endings are mostly grammatical.
intro.cn: bay 的派生词不多，词尾变化多表示语法。

latinIntro.en: The water sense goes back to Latin baia, a harbour.
latinIntro.cn: 水域义可追溯到拉丁语 baia「港湾」。

items.meaning: a sheltered part of the sea

definition_en: to take control of a place by force, or to succeed in dealing with something difficult
core_image: 一面旗插上城头，城门从里面被推开
scene: 登山队在暴风雪里坚持了三天，终于站上顶峰。 They conquered the peak on the third day.
sceneCN: 这里 conquer 指「克服；征服」（第 3 个义项：成功应对困难事物）；句意是他们在第三天登顶成功。

senses.title: Take by force
senses.definition: to take control of a place or a people by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力取得对某地或某群人的控制
senses.example: The empire tried to conquer the whole coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国试图征服整条海岸。
senses.why: A wall falls and the land behind it changes owner.
senses.whyCN: 城墙一倒，墙后的土地就换了主人。

senses.title: Defeat an enemy
senses.definition: to defeat an opponent in war or in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 在战争或竞争中击败对手
senses.example: They conquered every rival in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 他们战胜了该地区的每一个对手。
senses.why: The winner stands while the other side can no longer act.
senses.whyCN: 胜者站着，而另一方再也无力行动。

senses.title: Overcome a difficulty
senses.definition: to succeed in dealing with something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 成功应对困难的事物
senses.example: She conquered her fear of speaking in public.
senses.exampleCN: 她克服了当众讲话的恐惧。
senses.why: The same strength that takes a city can take a fear.
senses.whyCN: 能攻下一座城的力量，也能攻下一份恐惧。

intro.en: Conquer comes from Latin conquirere, to seek out and obtain, from com-, fully, and quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: conquer 来自拉丁语 conquirere，意为四处寻求并取得，由 com-（彻底）与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, ask or search for.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问、搜寻。

items.en: Conquirere meant to seek out thoroughly and collect.
items.cn: conquirere 意为彻底搜寻并收集。

items.en: In late Latin the word gained the military sense of winning ground.
items.cn: 在晚期拉丁语中，这个词获得了攻占土地的军事含义。

items.en: Old French conquere told of knights winning lands.
items.cn: 古法语 conquere 讲述骑士赢得土地的故事。

items.en: English conquer first meant to win by fighting.
items.cn: 英语 conquer 最初指靠打仗赢取。

items.en: It now also means to master a fear or a difficult skill.
items.cn: 如今它也指战胜恐惧或掌握一项难学的技能。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words confusingly close in sound or form, and the meaning group names other ways to win.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音或外形容易混淆的词，近义组列出其他表示赢取的说法。

entries.definition: to agree with someone
a person who takes land by force
the act of taking control by force
to win against an opponent
to succeed against a difficulty
to defeat completely in battle

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a flag on a wall, then move to a rival who yields and to a fear that is finally faced.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从城墙上的旗帜开始，再到让步的对手，最后到终于被面对的恐惧。

normal.en: Con- is fully and quer- is seek, so conquer is to seek until the thing is yours.
normal.cn: con- 是彻底，quer- 是寻求，conquer 就是一直寻求直到把东西拿到手。

normal.en: Divide and conquer: split the problem, then take each part.
normal.cn: 分而治之：先拆开问题，再逐个拿下。

normal.en: A flag on a wall is a conquest finished.
normal.cn: 城墙上的旗子，是一桩征服已经完成的标志。

normal.en: Fear is the city inside you, and courage is the army.
normal.cn: 恐惧是你心里的城，勇气就是那支军队。

normal.en: You conquer a mountain one step at a time, not in one leap.
normal.cn: 征服一座山要一步一步走，而不是一跃而上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a flag from a bag.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从袋子里抽出一面旗。

abstract.en: Picture a locked gate opening from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇锁着的门从里面被打开。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow shrinking as a person walks toward it.
abstract.cn: 想象人朝影子走去时，影子越缩越小。

examples.en: The army conquered the city within a week.
examples.cn: 军队在一周之内攻下了这座城市。

examples.en: She conquered her fear of the stage.
examples.cn: 她克服了对舞台的恐惧。

examples.en: He finally conquered the steep climb.
examples.cn: 他终于征服了这段陡坡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conquer 记成 con（彻底）加 quer（寻求）：一路追着目标不放，直到把城池或恐惧都拿下来。

root: 源自拉丁语 conquirere（com 彻底 + quaerere 寻求），本义是彻底搜寻取得，后转为以武力征服与克服困难。

sensesIntro.en: From an army taking a city, to a rival beaten, and finally to a private fear finally mastered.
sensesIntro.cn: 从军队攻下城池，到对手被击败，最后到私人恐惧终于被掌控。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a banner raised where another banner used to stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：在原先插着别家旗帜的地方，升起自己的旗。

branches.en: The first sense is land taken and held by force.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是靠武力夺取并守住的土地。

branches.en: The second sense is an opponent who can no longer resist.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是再也无力抵抗的对手。

branches.en: The third sense moves the battlefield inside the person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把战场移到了人的内心。

branches.en: Taking a place and beating its defenders are one act seen twice.
branches.cn: 占领一地与击败守军，是同一行为的两个侧面。

branches.en: The strength that beats an army can also beat a habit.
branches.cn: 能击败军队的力量，也能击败一个旧习惯。

intro.en: Conquer is built on Latin com-, fully, plus quaerere, to seek.
intro.cn: conquer 由拉丁语 com-（彻底）与 quaerere（寻求）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin seek base quer- also appears in query and quest, and in inquire and require.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的寻求词基 quer- 也出现在 query、quest、inquire 与 require 中。

items.meaning: to win something by force or effort
items.meaningCN: 凭武力或努力赢得某物

items.exampleCN: 征服者放过了这座城镇。

items.meaning: the act or result of conquering

items.exampleCN: 没有哪堵墙真的能被攻克。
她的精神始终无法被压服。

items.example: The quest for water lasted weeks.
items.exampleCN: 寻找水源的过程持续了数周。

definition_zh: 拥抱；欣然接受；包含；包围
definition_en: to hold someone closely in the arms; to accept an idea willingly; to include or contain
core_image: 两条手臂合拢，把一个人或一个念头整个圈进来
scene: 车站重逢，两人隔着人群张开手臂。 They embraced at the station after two years apart.
sceneCN: 这里 embrace 是「拥抱」（第 01 个义项：用双臂抱紧某人）；句意是分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。

pos.zh: 及物动词：拥抱；欣然接受；包含

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「拥抱；接受」（较少见）
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可拥抱的；可接受的」（较少见）
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「包容的；拥抱的」

senses.title: To hold someone in the arms
senses.definition: to put your arms around someone and hold them closely
senses.definitionCN: 用双臂环住某人并抱紧
senses.example: They embraced at the station after two years apart.
senses.exampleCN: 分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。
senses.why: The French source joins in- with brace, an arm, so the word's body is literally putting arms around someone.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源把 in-（在内）与 brace（手臂）结合，所以这个词的身体动作字面就是「把手臂环上去」。

senses.title: To accept an idea willingly
senses.definition: to accept a belief, change or opportunity with enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 热情地接受某种观念、变化或机会
senses.example: The company embraced the new technology.
senses.exampleCN: 公司欣然接受了这项新技术。
senses.why: An idea can be taken into the arms the way a person is, so embracing a plan means drawing it close instead of pushing it away.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能像人一样被抱进怀里，所以 embrace a plan 就是把计划拉近，而不是推开。

senses.title: To include or contain
senses.definition: to include something as part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为更大整体的一部分包含进来
senses.example: The course embraces both theory and practice.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课兼顾理论与实践。
senses.why: Arms that close around a group enclose everything inside, so the verb extends from hugging a person to containing a range of things.
senses.whyCN: 手臂合拢会把一群东西都圈在里面，于是这个动词从抱人扩展到涵盖一系列事物。

intro.en: Embrace came from Old French, where the word for arm supplied the picture of arms closing around something.
intro.cn: embrace 来自古法语，其中表示「手臂」的词提供了双臂合拢的画面。

items.en: Bracchium meant the forearm or arm.
items.cn: bracchium 意为前臂或手臂。

items.en: Brace meant an arm, and the verb embracier meant to put arms around.
items.cn: brace 意为手臂，动词 embracier 意为用双臂环抱。

items.en: English borrowed embrace in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 embrace。

items.en: The figurative sense of accepting an idea appeared.
items.cn: 表示接受某种观念的比喻义出现。

items.en: The verb now covers hugging, accepting and including.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个动词涵盖拥抱、接受与包含。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the arm root; the near-meaning group separates a hug, acceptance and inclusion.
note.cn: 形近组沿着「手臂」词根展开；近义组区分拥抱、接受与包含。

entries.definition: An ornament worn around the wrist, from the arm root.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「手链」，词根仍是「手臂」。

entries.definition: A support or pair, from the same Old French arm word.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，义为「支架、一对」，源自古法语的手臂词。

entries.definition: The act of embracing, a rare noun.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「拥抱、接受」，较少见。

entries.definition: To hold someone closely, the plain everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拥抱」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To agree to take something offered.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接受」，对应本词的观念义。

entries.definition: To have something as part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包含」，对应本词的涵盖义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read embrace as arms closing in, then let the same circle take in ideas and whole ranges.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 embrace 读成双臂合拢，再让同一个圆圈把观念与整片范围都圈进来。

normal.en: Em- plus brace, an arm: put arms around.
normal.cn: em- 加 brace（手臂）：把手臂环上去。

normal.en: A warm embrace is the plain physical sense.
normal.cn: warm embrace 就是最朴素的拥抱义。

normal.en: To embrace change is to hold it close.
normal.cn: embrace change 就是把变化抱近。

normal.en: A course that embraces theory and practice contains both.
normal.cn: embrace 两者的课程把二者都包含进来。

normal.en: Bracelet shares the same arm root.
normal.cn: bracelet 与本词共享「手臂」词根。

abstract.en: Picture two arms drawing a circle around a person or a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象两条手臂在一个人或一个计划周围画出一个圆圈。

abstract.en: The same gesture means welcome, agreement and containment.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作同时表示欢迎、同意与容纳。

abstract.en: Embrace is a hug that learned to hold ideas.
abstract.cn: embrace 就是一个学会了抱想法的拥抱。

examples.en: They embraced at the station after two years apart.
examples.cn: 分别两年后他们在车站拥抱。

examples.en: The company embraced the new technology.
examples.cn: 公司欣然接受了这项新技术。

examples.en: The course embraces both theory and practice.
examples.cn: 这门课兼顾理论与实践。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因不来死」——久别重逢，抱紧一点才不松开

root: 经古法语 embracier 借入，由 em-（在内）加 brace（手臂）构成；brace 源自拉丁语 bracchium（手臂）。

sensesIntro.en: Embrace begins with arms around a person, then draws ideas close, then encloses a whole range.
sensesIntro.cn: embrace 先用双臂抱住一个人，再把观念拉近，最后把一整片范围圈进来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arms drawing a closed circle around something.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条手臂合拢，把某物圈成一个闭合的圆。

branches.en: THE HUG: two people closing the circle.
branches.cn: 拥抱线：两个人把圆圈合上。

branches.en: THE IDEA: a plan drawn into the arms.
branches.cn: 观念线：把计划拉进怀里。

branches.en: THE RANGE: a whole set held inside the circle.
branches.cn: 范围线：把一整组事物圈在里面。

branches.en: BODY AND MIND: the same gesture welcomes a person and a thought.
branches.cn: 身与心：同一个动作既欢迎人，也欢迎想法。

branches.en: HOLD AND CONTAIN: arms that hug also enclose.
branches.cn: 抱与容：会拥抱的手臂也会围住。

intro.en: Embrace is a French borrowing built on brace, arm; English then added -ment and -able to make rare nouns and adjectives.
intro.cn: embrace 是建立在 brace（手臂）之上的法语借词；英语后来又加 -ment 与 -able 造出少见的名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bracchium, arm, is the recorded root behind the French word brace.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bracchium（手臂）是法语 brace 背后有记录的词根。

items.meaning: he does, or more than one

derivatives.zh: 可拥抱的；可接受的（较少见）

definition_en: large farm animals with horns and hooves, especially cows and bulls, kept for milk or meat
core_image: 成群低头吃草的牛，被人赶来赶去
scene: 清晨的草场上，牛群慢慢移动。 The farmer counted the cattle before opening the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 cattle 指「牛」（第 1 个义项：成群饲养的牛类家畜）；句意是农夫开栅门前先数了一遍牛。

senses.title: Cows and bulls kept on a farm
senses.definition: large domesticated animals of the cow family, kept in herds for milk, meat or work
senses.definitionCN: 牛科的大型家养动物，成群饲养以取奶、取肉或役用
senses.example: The cattle graze in the lower field.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群在低处的田里吃草。
senses.why: The core image is a herd of grazing animals, and that is what the word names today.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一群低头吃草的动物，这正是今天这个词所指。

senses.title: Farm livestock in general
senses.definition: farm animals kept as property, used in older or rural speech for livestock in general
senses.definitionCN: 作为财产饲养的家畜，在较早或乡村说法中泛指各类牲畜
senses.example: In old wills, cattle could include horses and sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧遗嘱里，cattle 可能也包括马和羊。
senses.why: The word first meant property, so any movable farm animal could once be counted as cattle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指财产，所以任何可移动的农家动物都曾被算作 cattle。

intro.en: Cattle first meant property in general, then movable goods, then farm animals, and only later cows in particular.
intro.cn: cattle 最初泛指财产，再指动产，再指农家牲畜，最后才专指牛。

items.en: Capitale meant property or wealth, from caput, head, the source of capital.
items.cn: 拉丁语 capitale 意为财产或财富，源自 caput（头），也是 capital 的来源。

items.en: Catel meant property, including livestock as the main movable wealth of a farm.
items.cn: 古法语 catel 指财产，其中牲畜是农家的主要动产。

items.en: Catel covers movable goods and farm animals, especially cows and oxen.
items.cn: 中古英语 catel 涵盖动产与农家牲畜，尤其是牛。

items.en: Cattle narrows to bovine animals as chattel takes over the legal sense of property.
items.cn: 随着 chattel 接管法律上的财产义，cattle 收窄为牛类。

items.en: Modern English keeps cattle as a plural collective with no singular form in use.
items.cn: 现代英语中 cattle 只作复数集合名词，日常不再有单数形式。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the old property root, while the meaning group lists farm animals and herds.
note.cn: 形近组沿古老的财产词根展开，近义组列出农家动物与畜群。

entries.definition: a person who raises or tends cattle
a dog trained to herd cattle
an item of movable personal property
farm animals kept for use or profit
entries.definitionCN: 为使用或获利而饲养的农家动物

entries.definition: a large group of animals feeding together
entries.definitionCN: 一起觅食的一大群动物

entries.definition: a castrated male cow used for work
entries.definitionCN: 阉割后用于劳作的公牛

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie cattle to capital, to chattel and to the collective plural it still is.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cattle 与 capital、chattel 以及它仍是集合复数这一点连起来。

normal.en: Cattle, capital and chattel all descend from a Latin word for property.
normal.cn: cattle、capital、chattel 都源自拉丁语中表示财产的词。

normal.en: Chattel is the legal cousin: cattle were once simply movable property with legs.
normal.cn: chattel 是法律上的表亲：cattle 曾经就是长了腿的动产。

normal.en: Dairy cattle and beef cattle split the same herd by purpose.
normal.cn: dairy cattle 与 beef cattle 按用途把同一群牛分开。

normal.en: Cattle has no ordinary singular, so one says a cow or a head of cattle.
normal.cn: cattle 没有日常单数，说一头牛要用 a cow 或 a head of cattle。

normal.en: A herd of cattle keeps the collective picture of many animals moving together.
normal.cn: a herd of cattle 保留了众多动物一起移动的群像。

abstract.en: Picture slow brown backs moving through morning mist.
abstract.cn: 想象晨雾中缓缓移动的一片棕色牛背。

abstract.en: Picture a dog running low behind a straggling herd.
abstract.cn: 想象一条狗低身跑在散开的牛群后面。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer counting heads at a wooden gate.
abstract.cn: 想象农夫在木栅门边数着牛的头数。

examples.en: The cattle were moved to a larger field.
examples.cn: 牛群被赶到更大的田里。

examples.en: He has worked with dairy cattle all his life.
examples.cn: 他一生都在和奶牛打交道。

examples.en: A herd of cattle blocked the road.
examples.cn: 一群牛堵住了路。

dict_mnemonic.text: cattle 与 capital 同源：从前牛就是最值钱的家当，所以「牛」这个词里藏着「财产」。

root: 源自古法语 catel（财产），上溯拉丁语 capitale（财产、财富），与 capital、chattel 同根，词义由财产收窄为牛。

sensesIntro.en: Property becomes livestock, livestock becomes cows, and an older rural use still covers farm animals in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 财产变成牲畜，牲畜变成牛，而较旧的乡村用法仍泛指农家动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herd of grazing animals, the farmer's movable wealth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群吃草的牲畜，也就是农家的动产财富。

branches.en: The everyday sense keeps the grazing herd of cows and bulls.

definition_en: having the power to attract iron, or relating to magnets, magnetic fields and the force they produce
core_image: 一块黑色矿石隔着白纸把铁屑排成一道道弧线，纸下什么都没有，铁屑却自己排队
scene: 实验室的白纸上，一块黑色矿石压着薄薄一层铁屑，铁屑自己排成弧线，围观的人都屏住了呼吸。 A magnetic mineral draws iron filings into curved lines even through a sheet of paper.
sceneCN: 这里 magnetic 指「具有吸引铁、能产生磁场的性质」（第 1 个义项：能够吸引铁并形成磁场）；句意为一块有磁性的矿石隔着白纸也能把铁屑吸成弧线。图中可辨识物件：黑色矿石、白纸、铁屑、放大镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有磁性的；磁的；靠磁力工作的
有魅力的；有强烈吸引力的

senses.title: Attracting iron
senses.definition: having the property of attracting iron and producing a magnetic field around itself
senses.definitionCN: 具有吸引铁并在周围产生磁场的性质
senses.example: A magnetic rod lifted every nail from the bench in one sweep.
senses.exampleCN: 一根有磁性的棒子一扫，就把工作台上的钉子全吸了起来。
senses.why: The word names the property that first made a certain ore famous: iron moves toward it although nothing visible pulls.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是让某种矿石最早出名的性质：看不见任何东西在拉，铁却朝它移动。

senses.title: Belonging to the study of magnets
senses.titleCN: 与磁学、磁力研究有关的
senses.definition: relating to magnetism as a subject of scientific study
senses.definitionCN: 与作为科学研究对象的磁学、磁力有关
senses.example: Her thesis examines the magnetic behaviour of thin films.
senses.exampleCN: 她的论文研究薄膜的磁性行为。
senses.why: Once the stone became an object of experiment, the adjective shifted from the object to the whole field of inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 当磁石成为实验对象之后，这个形容词就从物件本身转到了整个研究领域。

senses.title: Driven by magnetic force
senses.definition: operated or produced by magnetic forces rather than by direct contact
senses.definitionCN: 靠磁力而非直接接触来运转或产生
senses.example: The magnetic levitation train floats above its guideway.
senses.exampleCN: 磁悬浮列车悬浮在导轨上方。
senses.why: If a stone can move iron without touching it, that pull can also be harnessed to lift a whole train.
senses.whyCN: 既然磁石不接触就能移动铁，这股拉力自然也就能用来托起整列火车。

senses.title: Of a planet's field
senses.definition: relating to the natural field generated by a planet or a star
senses.definitionCN: 与行星或恒星自然产生的磁场有关
senses.example: Migrating birds appear to read the magnetic field of the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 迁徙的鸟似乎能读取地球的磁场。
senses.why: The same invisible influence surrounds the whole planet, so the adjective applies to fields far larger than any stone.
senses.whyCN: 同一种看不见的作用笼罩整个行星，于是这个词也用于比任何磁石都大得多的场。

senses.title: Storing data in magnetized material
senses.definition: using magnetized material to record and keep information
senses.definitionCN: 用被磁化的材料记录并保存信息
senses.example: The old magnetic tape still holds the studio recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 那卷旧磁带里还存着当年的录音。
senses.why: A magnet can fix a pattern in iron particles, and a fixed pattern can carry a signal, so magnetism became a way to write memory.
senses.whyCN: 磁体能在铁微粒里固定下一道图案，而固定图案可以承载信号，于是磁性成了写入记忆的手段。

senses.title: Having two opposite poles
senses.titleCN: 分南北极、同极相斥异极相吸
senses.definition: having north and south poles that attract and repel one another
senses.definitionCN: 具有南北两极，同极相斥、异极相吸
senses.example: Two magnetic poles of the same kind push each other away.
senses.exampleCN: 两个同类的磁极会把对方推开。
senses.why: The pull is never single: it always comes in a pair of opposite ends, which is why the adjective also describes polarity.
senses.whyCN: 这种拉力从不单独出现，总是成对的两端，因此这个词也用来描述极性。

senses.title: Charming a room
senses.definition: having a personality that draws people strongly and willingly
senses.definitionCN: 具有让人不由自主被吸引的个性
senses.example: Her magnetic presence made the whole room quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 她那种有磁性的气场让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the stone's invisible pull: nothing is said or forced, yet attention turns toward the person.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了磁石看不见的拉力：没有言语也没有强迫，注意力却转向那个人。

senses.title: An abstract pull
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不可抗拒的吸引力
senses.definition: exerting an attraction so strong that it feels physical
senses.definitionCN: 施加一种强到近乎物理层面的吸引
senses.example: The magnetic appeal of the old city keeps artists returning.
senses.exampleCN: 老城那种不可抗拒的吸引力让艺术家一再回来。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the stone: what is attracted is no longer iron but a person, a memory or a whole crowd.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把磁石一般化：被吸引的不再是铁，而是人、记忆或一整群人。

intro.en: Magnetic goes back to the Greek name of a stone from Magnesia, through Latin magnes and the later Latin adjective magneticus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: magnetic 经拉丁 magnes 与晚期拉丁形容词 magneticus，上溯希腊语中一种来自马格尼西亚的石头之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Magnētis lithos, 'the stone of Magnesia', named a naturally magnetized iron ore. The place-name explanation is generally accepted, but the origin of the place name itself is not settled.
items.cn: magnētis lithos 意为「马格尼西亚的石头」，指一种天然带磁性的铁矿石。以地名解释这一石名一般认为是可行的，但地名本身的来源没有定论。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as magnes, genitive magnetis, and later formed the adjective magneticus from the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词，作 magnes，属格 magnetis；后来又用同一词干构成形容词 magneticus。

items.en: English magnet is recorded in the thirteenth century through Old French magnete, and the adjective magnetic follows in the sixteenth.
items.cn: 英语 magnet 在十三世纪经古法语 magnete 出现，形容词 magnetic 则到十六世纪才跟上。

items.en: From the sixteenth century magnetic described the invisible influence itself, and magnetic field became standard after Faraday's experiments in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，magnetic 开始描述那种看不见的作用本身；到十九世纪法拉第的实验之后，magnetic field 成为标准说法。

items.en: Animal magnetism, the theory Franz Mesmer promoted in the 1770s, supplied the metaphor of a person who draws others like iron to a lodestone.
items.cn: 梅斯默在十八世纪七十年代推崇的「动物磁力」理论，提供了「人像铁被磁石吸引」这一比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (place name and first record): the link to Magnesia is generally accepted, yet the origin of the place name and the exact earliest English citation of magnetic remain unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（地名与首见记录）：与马格尼西亚的联系一般认为是成立的，但地名的来源以及 magnetic 最早的确切英语书证仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same magnet stem, plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds words for the pull itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 magnet 词干的词，另加一个形近却异源的词；第二组是表示「吸引力」本身的词。

entries.definition: The stone or device itself; magnetic is the adjective made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 磁石或磁体本身；magnetic 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The property or the science, not the object; the ending -ism marks a state or system.
entries.definitionCN: 指性质或学科，而不是物件；-ism 后缀标记状态或体系。

entries.definition: The black iron ore that can be magnetized; the ending -ite marks a mineral.
entries.definitionCN: 能被磁化的黑色铁矿石；-ite 后缀标记矿物。

entries.definition: A powerful person in business or industry, from Latin magnus 'great'; it shares spelling only, not ancestry.
entries.definitionCN: 商业或工业界的权贵，来自拉丁 magnus「大的」；只同拼写，并不同源。

entries.definition: Pleasing enough to draw interest, used of looks or offers; it carries no hint of a field.
entries.definitionCN: 足够讨喜而引来兴趣，多用于外貌或条件；不含磁场的意味。

entries.definition: Able to inspire followers through force of personality; narrower than magnetic and mainly about leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 靠人格力量鼓舞追随者；比 magnetic 窄，主要用于领袖。

entries.definition: Attractive in a way that promises pleasure or gain; it suggests enticement rather than natural pull.
entries.definitionCN: 以快乐或利益诱人的；偏「引诱」而非自然吸引。

entries.definition: So absorbing that attention cannot leave it; stronger and stranger than magnetic.
entries.definitionCN: 吸引人到无法移开注意；比 magnetic 更强也更奇异。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real stem, the real compounds and the real phrases of the magnet family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的词干、真实的复合词，以及磁石词族里真实存在的搭配。

normal.en: The stem is the name of a stone from Magnesia, so magnet came before magnetism and magnetic.
normal.cn: 词干来自马格尼西亚的一种石头之名，因此先有 magnet，才有 magnetism 与 magnetic。

normal.en: The family runs magnet, magnetism, magnetize, magnetite, electromagnet and magnetometer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 magnet、magnetism、magnetize、magnetite、electromagnet 与 magnetometer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: magnetic field, magnetic pole, magnetic force, magnetic compass.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：磁场、磁极、磁力、磁罗盘。

normal.en: The same adjective serves the metaphor: a magnetic personality draws people the way a stone draws pins.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词也承担比喻：有魅力的个性吸人，正如磁石吸针。

normal.en: Electricity and magnetism sit side by side: electromagnet joins electro- to magnet.
normal.cn: 电与磁并肩而立：electromagnet 由 electro- 与 magnet 拼成。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible hand under the paper: the filings line up though nothing touches them.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下有一只无形的手：没有东西碰到铁屑，它们却排好了队。

abstract.en: Picture two ends that cannot be separated: cut the bar in half and each half still has a north and a south.
abstract.cn: 想象两个无法分开的端点：把磁条切成两半，每一半仍有南极和北极。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting toward one speaker without being told to move.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人没有接到任何指令，却慢慢朝同一个演讲者靠过去。

examples.en: The magnetic strip on the card was worn, so the machine could not read it.
examples.cn: 卡片上的磁条磨损了，机器读不出来。

examples.en: Iron is strongly magnetic, while copper barely responds at all.
examples.cn: 铁有很强的磁性，而铜几乎毫无反应。

examples.en: The campaign gained magnetic force once the young mayor joined it.
examples.cn: 年轻市长加入之后，这场运动有了强大的吸引力。

dict_mnemonic.text: magnet（磁石）+ -ic（形容词后缀）——像磁石那样会吸 → 有磁性的；也有吸引力

root: 希腊语 magnētis lithos（马格尼西亚的石头）→ 拉丁 magnes/magnetis → 拉丁形容词 magneticus → 英语 magnetic；地名来源一般认为是，地名本身来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a stone pulling iron, pass through field, machine and stored data, and end with the pull a person or a place exerts on a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一块吸铁的石头出发，经过磁场、机器与存储的数据，最后落到一个人或一个地方对人群的吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone moves iron across a sheet of paper without ever touching it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头隔着纸移动铁，却从不接触它。

branches.en: The stone and its poles: attraction and repulsion are two faces of one property.
branches.cn: 磁石与其两极：吸与斥是同一种性质的两张脸。

branches.en: From property to force: what the physicist measures is what the machine harnesses.
branches.cn: 从性质到力：物理学家测量的，正是机器所利用的。

branches.en: The planet itself as one huge magnet with a field around it.
branches.cn: 行星本身就是一块巨大的磁铁，外面罩着一层场。

branches.en: The pull fixed into matter as a pattern that can be read back.
branches.cn: 把拉力固定进物质，变成可以读回的图案。

branches.en: The same pull felt between people, or toward a place or an idea.
branches.cn: 同样的拉力发生在人与人之间，或指向一个地方、一个念头。

intro.en: Magnetic is an adjective built on the noun magnet with the Latin suffix -ic, so the whole family reads outward from the stone.
intro.cn: magnetic 是名词 magnet 加拉丁形容词后缀 -ic 构成，整个词族都可以从磁石向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin magnes, genitive magnetis, came from Greek magnēs; New Latin added magnetismus for the property, and English built the rest on that stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 magnes（属格 magnetis）来自希腊 magnēs；新拉丁语又加 magnetismus 表示性质，英语其余词都建在这个词干上。

items.meaning: a stone or device that attracts iron
items.example: The magnet held the note to the steel door.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁把便条吸在钢门上。

items.meaning: of a magnet; able to attract
items.meaningCN: 磁的；有吸引力的（加形容词后缀，由物件转为性质）
items.example: The magnetic field bends the beam.

items.meaning: the property of magnets; the science of it
items.meaningCN: 磁性；磁学（加状态后缀，由物件转为性质与学科）
items.exampleCN: 磁性感住了博物学家好几个世纪。

items.meaningCN: 使磁化（加动词后缀，表示使成为）
items.example: The current magnetizes the iron core.

items.meaning: the process or degree of becoming magnetic
items.meaningCN: 磁化过程或磁化程度（再加名词后缀，表示过程与结果）
items.example: Magnetization reverses as the current alternates.
items.exampleCN: 电流交变时，磁化方向随之反转。

items.meaning: the black iron ore that magnets occur in
items.meaningCN: 磁铁矿（加矿物后缀，由性质转到具体矿石）
items.example: Magnetite lies in bands along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 磁铁矿沿着山脊成带状分布。

items.meaning: a magnet worked by an electric coil
items.meaningCN: 电磁铁（由「电」与人造磁体复合，动力来源改变）
items.example: The electromagnet drops the load when switched off.
items.exampleCN: 断电时电磁铁把货物放下。

items.meaning: an instrument for measuring magnetic strength
items.meaningCN: 磁强计（加测量器械后缀，由性质转为量具）
items.example: The survey used a magnetometer over the wreck.
items.exampleCN: 勘测时用磁强计扫过沉船。

items.meaningCN: 非磁性的（加否定前缀，性质被取消）
items.example: The case is made of nonmagnetic steel.

latinEntries.meaning: the region that gave the stone its name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 给这种石头命名的那一地区

definition_en: to become larger or rounder, or to increase in size or amount
core_image: 扭伤的脚踝慢慢鼓起一个包
scene: 他的脚踝扭伤后肿了起来。 His ankle began to swell after the fall.
sceneCN: 这里 swell 是「肿胀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的脚踝扭伤后肿了起来。

senses.title: To become swollen
senses.definition: to become larger or rounder, often from injury
senses.definitionCN: 因受伤等变大或鼓起
senses.example: His ankle began to swell after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他的脚踝扭伤后肿了起来。
senses.why: This is the bodily sense of swelling.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体肿胀的义项。

senses.title: To increase in size
senses.definition: to grow larger in number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量或规模变大
senses.example: The crowd swelled to thousands.
senses.exampleCN: 人群增加到数千人。
senses.why: The body image extends to crowds and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 身体形象扩展到人群与数量。

senses.title: A rolling wave
senses.definition: a slow rolling movement of the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海面缓慢起伏的涌动
senses.example: A slow swell rocked the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的涌浪摇动着小船。
senses.why: The noun names a rising movement.
senses.whyCN: 名词指一种升起的运动。

intro.en: Swell is an old Germanic verb for growing larger.
intro.cn: swell 是表示变大的古老日耳曼动词。

items.en: Swellan meant to grow.
items.cn: swellan 意为增大。

items.en: Swellan meant to swell.
items.cn: swellan 意为肿胀。

items.en: Swelle meant to become larger.
items.cn: swelle 意为变大。

items.en: Swell described injury and crowds.
items.cn: swell 描述受伤与人群。

items.en: Swell became a noun for sea movement.
items.cn: swell 成为表示海面涌动的名词。

note.en: Swell is compared with look-alike words and with words for growing larger.
note.cn: 把 swell 与形近词以及表示变大的词作比较。

to sense an odor
to write letters in order
to become larger
to fill with air
to stick out

normalIntro.en: Swell is growth that pushes outward.
normalIntro.cn: swell 是向外推的增大。

normal.en: His ankle began to swell after the fall.
normal.cn: 他的脚踝扭伤后肿了起来。

normal.en: The crowd swelled to thousands.
normal.cn: 人群增加到数千人。

normal.en: Her heart swelled with pride.
normal.cn: 她心中充满自豪。

normal.en: A slow swell rocked the boat.
normal.cn: 缓慢的涌浪摇动着小船。

normal.en: The river swelled after the rain.
normal.cn: 雨后河水上涨了。

abstract.en: Swell is size answering an inner pressure.
abstract.cn: 肿胀是体积回应内在压力。

abstract.en: Pride can swell a heart without adding weight.
abstract.cn: 自豪能让心膨胀而不增重量。

abstract.en: The sea breathes in long swells.
abstract.cn: 大海以长长的涌动呼吸。

examples.en: His ankle began to swell after the fall.

examples.en: The crowd swelled to thousands.

root: 来自古英语 swellan（肿胀），源于日耳曼语 swellan。

sensesIntro.en: Swell means to become larger, to increase, or a rolling sea movement.
sensesIntro.cn: swell 表示肿胀、增大，或海面涌动。

core.en: Something pressing outward from inside.
core.cn: 某物从内部向外挤压。

branches.en: His ankle began to swell after the fall.
branches.cn: 他的脚踝扭伤后肿了起来。

branches.en: Her eyes were swollen with tears.
branches.cn: 她哭得眼睛都肿了。

branches.en: The crowd swelled to thousands.
branches.cn: 人群增加到数千人。

branches.en: A slow swell rocked the boat.
branches.cn: 缓慢的涌浪摇动着小船。

branches.en: Bodies and crowds can both swell.
branches.cn: 身体与人群都能膨胀。

intro.en: Swell forms swelled, swollen and the noun swelling.
intro.cn: swell 构成 swelled、swollen 以及名词 swelling。

latinIntro.en: Swell is Germanic; Latin tumere, to swell, lies behind tumor.
latinIntro.cn: swell 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 tumere（肿胀）是 tumor 的来源。

definition_zh: 青春期；青春期阶段；少年时期；发育过渡期；青春期的身心变化；青春期人群；青春期的社会阶段；生理成熟期
definition_en: the period of life between childhood and adulthood, when a young person develops physically and emotionally
core_image: 一棵正在抽条的树苗：枝干突然拔高，树皮还没变硬，风一吹就晃
scene: 夏夜的院子里，蝉声不停，几个十几岁的孩子在灯下写作业。 During adolescence, sleep patterns often shift later in the evening.
sceneCN: 这里 adolescence 是「青春期」（第 1 个义项：童年与成年之间的成长阶段）；句意为在青春期，睡眠节律常常在晚上向后推迟。

pos.zh: 名词：青春期；青少年时期；发育过渡阶段

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语现在分词 adolescens 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「青春期的」
由形容词 adolescent 转类为零派生名词，义为「青少年」
由 adolescent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以青春期的方式」，较少使用

senses.title: The period between childhood and adulthood
senses.titleCN: 青春期：童年与成年之间的时期
senses.definition: the period of life between childhood and adulthood, when a person grows toward maturity
senses.definitionCN: 童年与成年之间的生命阶段，人在此期间走向成熟
senses.example: Adolescence is often described as a bridge between childhood and adulthood.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期常被描述为连接童年与成年的桥梁。
senses.why: The core image is a sapling shooting up: the stem lengthens fast while the bark is still soft.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一棵迅速抽条的树苗：树干猛长，树皮还很软。

senses.title: The stage studied in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学意义上的青春期阶段
senses.definition: the developmental stage that psychology studies as a distinct period of mental growth
senses.definitionCN: 心理学作为一个独立的心智成长阶段来研究的时期
senses.example: Psychologists treat adolescence as a stage with its own tasks and conflicts.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家把青春期看作一个有自身任务与冲突的阶段。
senses.why: The sapling is now observed rather than merely seen: the growth is divided into stages with names.
senses.whyCN: 树苗这时不只是被看见，而是被观察：生长被划分成有名称的阶段。

senses.title: The teenage years
senses.titleCN: 少年时期：十几岁的年月
senses.definition: the years of a person's teens, counted in ordinary speech rather than in theory
senses.definitionCN: 一个人十几岁的那几年，是日常说法而非理论划分
senses.example: She spent her adolescence in a small coastal town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的少年时期是在一个海边小镇度过的。
senses.why: Here the period is simply the stretch of years a person can point back to.
senses.whyCN: 这里的阶段就是一个人回头能指认出的那一段年月。

senses.title: A transitional period of growth
senses.definition: the transitional period in which a child's body and mind pass toward adult form
senses.definitionCN: 儿童的身体与心智向成年形态过渡的时期
senses.example: The clinic monitors growth throughout adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所会在整个发育过渡期监测生长情况。
senses.why: The sapling is between two states: no longer a seedling, not yet a full tree.
senses.whyCN: 树苗处在两种状态之间：不再是幼苗，也还不是成树。

senses.title: The bodily and emotional changes of that period
senses.definition: the physical and emotional changes that occur during this period
senses.definitionCN: 在这一时期发生的身体与情绪方面的变化
senses.example: Rapid mood shifts are common in early adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 情绪快速起伏在青春期早期很常见。
senses.why: What is named here is not the time but what fills it: growth shows itself as change.
senses.whyCN: 这里命名的不是那段时间，而是填满它的东西：成长以变化的形式显现。

senses.title: Young people of that age as a group
senses.definition: young people of this age considered together as a social group
senses.definitionCN: 把这一年龄段的年轻人作为一个社会群体来看待
senses.example: The survey asked adolescents about health, school and family.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查询问了青春期人群关于健康、学校与家庭的情况。
senses.why: Many saplings standing together become a grove: the stage turns into a group.
senses.whyCN: 许多树苗站在一起就成了林子：阶段变成了人群。

senses.title: The social stage between child and adult roles
senses.definition: the social stage in which a person is no longer treated as a child but not yet as an adult
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不再被当作孩子、却还未被当作成年人的社会阶段
senses.example: In many societies adolescence is marked by new duties and fewer protections.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多社会里，青春期的标志是新的责任与更少的保护。
senses.why: The sapling has its own place in the orchard: the period is also a position in society.
senses.whyCN: 树苗在果园里有自己的位置：这个时期也是一种社会位置。

senses.title: The period ending in physical maturity
senses.titleCN: 生理成熟期：以身体成熟告终
senses.definition: the span of growth that ends when the body reaches full physical maturity
senses.definitionCN: 以身体达到完全生理成熟为终点的生长期
senses.example: Bone growth is usually complete by the end of adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 骨骼生长通常在青春期结束时完成。

intro.en: Adolescence comes from Latin adolescentia, a noun of growing, and it still names growth rather than a fixed age.
intro.cn: adolescence 来自拉丁语 adolescentia，是一个表示「生长」的名词，至今指的生长过程而非固定年龄。

items.en: alescere was an inceptive verb meaning 'to begin to grow'; its stem is related to alere 'to nourish'.
items.cn: alescere 是一个表示「开始生长」的起始动词，其词干与 alere「滋养」有关。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus alescere gave adolescere, 'to grow up, come to maturity'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大、成熟起来」。

items.en: The noun adolescentia meant 'youth, the time of growing up'; its exact first use is not recorded.
items.cn: 名词 adolescentia 意为「青年时期、成长的年月」；其确切的首见用例没有记录。

items.en: English borrowed the word through French, using it for the age of youth rather than for a single person.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入这个词，用来指青年的年岁，而不是指某一个人。

items.en: Medicine and psychology gave the period clearer boundaries, and the word now names a stage of development.
items.cn: 医学与心理学为这个时期划出更清晰的边界，这个词如今指一个发育阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same growing root; the near-meaning group gathers other names for youth and its end point.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「生长」词根的一族词；近义组收其他表示青年及成熟终点的词。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective for a young person in this stage, or something typical of it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「青少年」或「青春期的」，指处在这一阶段的年轻人或其特征。

entries.definition: A grown person; Latin adultus is the past participle of the same verb 'to grow up'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年人」；拉丁语 adultus 正是同一个「长大」动词的过去分词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in the manner of an adolescent; rare.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以青少年的方式」，较少使用。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning reaching puberty; it looks close but comes from Latin pubes, not from alescere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「进入青春期的」；看起来相近，却来自拉丁语 pubes，与 alescere 无关。

entries.definition: The biological process of becoming sexually mature; narrower and more physical than adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春期、发身期」，指性成熟的过程，比 adolescence 更窄、更偏生理。

entries.definition: The time of being young, or young people collectively; broader and often warmer in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「青春、青年」，可指年轻时期或青年群体，范围更宽，语气常更温暖。

entries.definition: The years from thirteen to nineteen; a plain count of age rather than a stage of growth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十几岁」，只是对年龄的朴素计数，而不是成长阶段的划分。

entries.definition: The state reached at the end of growth; the far side of adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成熟」，是生长结束时所达到的状态，正位于青春期之后。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of growing up and the family it produced.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语「长大」动词，以及它产生的词族。

normal.en: alescere means to begin to grow, so adolescence is the time when growing takes hold.
normal.cn: alescere 意为「开始生长」，所以 adolescence 就是生长真正发力的那段时期。

normal.en: Adolescent, adult and adolescence all descend from the same verb adolescere.
normal.cn: adolescent、adult、adolescence 都来自同一个动词 adolescere。

normal.en: Adolescence names the period, while adolescent names the person; the ending -ence marks a state.
normal.cn: adolescence 指那段时期，adolescent 指那个人；词尾 -ence 标记一种状态。

normal.en: Puberty is the physical core of adolescence, not a synonym for the whole stage.
normal.cn: puberty 是青春期的生理核心，并不等于整个阶段的同义词。

normal.en: Early adolescence and late adolescence split the same growth into two ends.
normal.cn: early adolescence 与 late adolescence 把同一段成长分成首尾两端。

abstract.en: Picture a young tree that has suddenly grown taller than the fence, yet still bends in a strong wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵小树突然长得比篱笆还高，却仍会被大风压弯。

abstract.en: The tree is neither seedling nor timber: that in-between state is the whole idea of adolescence.
abstract.cn: 这棵树既不是幼苗也不是木材：这种不上不下的状态，正是青春期这一概念的核心。

abstract.en: A whole grove of such trees is the age group; when the bark finally hardens, the period is over.
abstract.cn: 一整片这样的小树就是这一年龄群体；当树皮终于变硬，这段时期就结束了。

examples.en: During adolescence, friendships often matter more than almost anything else.
examples.cn: 在青春期，友谊常常比几乎任何东西都重要。

examples.en: She spent her adolescence in a small coastal town.
examples.cn: 她的少年时期是在一个海边小镇度过的。

examples.en: The study follows children through adolescence into adult life.
examples.cn: 这项研究追踪孩子们从青春期一直到成年生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sapling shoots up fast while its bark is still soft and bends in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：树苗迅速拔高，树皮仍软，随风弯下。

branches.en: THE YEARS: the period itself and the plain stretch of teen years a person remembers.
branches.cn: 年月线：时期本身，以及一个人能回忆起的、朴素的十几岁岁月。

branches.en: THE STAGE: a named developmental step and the in-between transition of body and mind.
branches.cn: 阶段线：一个有名称的发育步骤，以及身心不上不下的过渡。

branches.en: THE BODY: the changes that fill the period, and the physical maturity that ends it.
branches.cn: 身体线：填满这段时期的变化，以及为它收尾的生理成熟。

branches.en: THE GROUP: many saplings standing together become a social category.
branches.cn: 群体线：许多树苗站在一起，就成为一个社会类别。

branches.en: THE POSITION: the stage is also a place in society, between child and adult roles.
branches.cn: 位置线：这个阶段也是社会中的一个位置，介于孩子与成人的角色之间。

definition_zh: 精神上；心理上；在脑中；智力上
definition_en: in the mind or in thought, rather than in the body, on paper or out loud
core_image: 灯下的人把纸笔都收进抽屉，整道题的步骤全在脑子里走
scene: 深夜的考场里，纸笔都收进了抽屉，几个学生闭着眼，把整道题的步骤在心里重走一遍。 She ran the whole route mentally before she set foot on the track.
sceneCN: 这里 mentally 是「在脑中、在心里默想」（第 2 个义项：不写不念地在脑内进行）；句意为她踏上跑道之前，先在脑子里把整条路线走了一遍。

senses.title: In the mind rather than in the body
senses.definition: in a person's mind or thoughts, as opposed to the body or the physical side
senses.definitionCN: 在人的心智或思绪层面，与身体、体力相对
senses.example: He was mentally tired long before his legs gave out.
senses.exampleCN: 他的腿还没垮，人已经在精神上累透了。
senses.why: The adverb is built on the Latin noun for mind, so it always reports what happens inside the head while the limbs may be doing nothing at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词建立在拉丁语中表示心智的名词上，所以它报告的总是脑袋里发生的事，而四肢可能什么都没做。

senses.title: Inside the head, with nothing written or spoken
senses.definition: by thinking or calculating silently, without writing anything down or saying the steps aloud
senses.definitionCN: 在脑子里默想、默算，不写下来，也不把步骤念出声
senses.example: She multiplied the figures mentally and nodded.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那几个数字在心里乘了一遍，然后点了点头。
senses.why: Here the mind is not only where the work happens but the only tool used, so the adverb moves from naming a place to naming a method.
senses.whyCN: 这里脑子不只是事情发生的地点，还是唯一被使用的工具，于是副词从指出地点转为指出方法。

senses.title: In the area of intelligence and reasoning
senses.definition: in the field of thinking and reasoning, especially when a task is measured against physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 在思考与推理的层面，尤用于把一项任务与体力消耗作对比
senses.example: The job is mentally demanding but physically light.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作费脑子，但不太费体力。
senses.why: A mind can be worked as hard as a muscle, so this sense weighs a task by the thinking it takes instead of by the weight it moves.
senses.whyCN: 脑子可以像肌肉一样被使到极限，所以这个义项用耗多少思考来衡量任务，而不是用搬动多少重量。

intro.en: Mentally is an English adverb built from the Latin noun for mind. Its history is short and plain: a Latin stem, a Late Latin adjective, and an English suffix of manner.
