items.en: Mentalis was formed on that stem with a suffix of relation, so it meant belonging to the mind.
items.cn: mentalis 在这个词干上加了表关系的后缀，意为属于心智的。

items.en: English borrowed mental in the medieval period for whatever belonged to the mind, and it was regularly set against bodily.
items.cn: 英语在中古时期借入 mental，指属于心智的一切，并经常与「身体的」相对使用。

items.en: The suffix -ly turned that adjective into an adverb of manner, so the new word answered how something was done, in the mind.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把这个形容词变成方式副词，新词回答的是「以何种方式」，即「在心里」。

items.en: Modern English applies the adverb to illness, effort, rehearsal and arithmetic, always marking the mind as the place where the action goes on.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个副词用在疾病、努力、预演和算术上，始终把心智标记为动作进行的地点。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem for mind and one word that only resembles it; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for thinking, feeling and the inner life.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「心智」的拉丁词干展开，另收一个只是形似的词；近义组收表示思考、感受与内心活动的副词。

entries.definition: Of or belonging to the mind.
A settled way of thinking shared by a person or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人或一群人固定的思维方式。

entries.definition: A trusted adviser; it only looks close and comes from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 值得信赖的指导者；只是拼写与 mental 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In terms of the working of the mind and emotions.
entries.definitionCN: 从心理与情绪的运作来看。

entries.definition: In terms of reasoning and understanding.
In terms of mental processes such as memory and judgement, used in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 就记忆、判断等心智过程而言，多用于学术文字。

entries.definition: In terms of feeling rather than thought.

normalIntro.en: This adverb is a small machine of three parts, a Latin stem for mind, a Latin ending, and an English ending that makes adverbs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词是一台三件组成的小机器：表示心智的拉丁词干、一个拉丁词尾，以及一个把词变成副词的英语词尾。

normal.en: Mens is Latin for mind, so mentally always marks the head as the place where something happens.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mens 意为心智，所以 mentally 总是把脑袋标成事情发生的地点。

normal.en: Mental is the adjective and -ly makes it an adverb of manner, so the pair answers what kind and in what way.
normal.cn: mental 是形容词，-ly 把它变成方式副词，于是这一对词一个回答「何种」，一个回答「如何」。

normal.en: Mentality is the noun for a whole settled outlook, while mentally describes a single act of thinking.
normal.cn: mentality 指一整套固定的看法，而 mentally 描述一次具体的思考。

normal.en: Mentally ill and mentally disabled are fixed phrases in medicine and law, where the adverb modifies the state rather than the action.
normal.cn: mentally ill 与 mentally disabled 是医学和法律里的固定说法，副词修饰的是状态而非动作。

normal.en: Mentally demanding weighs a task by thinking, just as physically demanding weighs it by the body.
normal.cn: mentally demanding 用思考量一项任务，正如 physically demanding 用身体来量。

abstract.en: The word quietly insists that a person can be worn out while sitting perfectly still.
abstract.cn: 这个词静静坚持一件事：一个人可以完全坐着不动，却已经被用尽。

abstract.en: A route walked in the head before it is walked on the ground says that rehearsal is a real form of doing.
abstract.cn: 先在心里走一遍、再落到地面上走，说明预演本身就是一种真实的行动。

abstract.en: Because the adverb names only the place, never the content, it can hold grief, arithmetic and memory in one small word.
abstract.cn: 因为这个副词只说出地点、从不说出内容，它才能用小小一个词同时装下悲伤、算术与记忆。

examples.en: He counted the change mentally before handing over the note.
examples.cn: 他把零钱在心里算了一遍，才把纸币递过去。

examples.en: She stayed mentally alert through the whole night shift.
examples.cn: 整个夜班期间，她的头脑一直保持清醒。

examples.en: The course is mentally demanding but easy on the legs.
examples.cn: 这门课很费脑子，但对腿脚没什么负担。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「门特利」——门里特别亮的那盏灯，照的是脑子；记住 mentally 是精神上、在心里。

root: 拉丁语 mens（心智，词干 ment-）→ 晚期拉丁语 mentalis（属于心智的）→ 英语 mental（精神的）+ -ly（方式副词词尾）→ mentally。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mind as the place where something happens. From there the adverb divides into a state, a silent method, and a measure of how much thinking a task costs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把心智当作事情发生的地点。副词由此分出三种用法：一种状态、一种不出声的方法，以及衡量任务耗多少思考的尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit desk with the paper pushed aside and all the work going on behind the eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯亮着，纸被推到一边，所有活都在眼睛后面进行。

branches.en: a tired face long before tired legs
branches.cn: 人先累在脸上，腿还没累

branches.en: figures moving behind closed eyes
branches.cn: 闭着眼在脑中走过一串数字

branches.en: a desk cleared of paper and pen
branches.cn: 桌上纸笔都收起来了

branches.en: a mind worn out while the body sits still
branches.cn: 身体坐着不动，脑子已经用尽

branches.en: a worker finishing the sum without a single note
branches.cn: 干活的人一张纸都没用就解完了

intro.en: The word is assembled from a Latin noun of mind, a Latin suffix of relation, and an English suffix that turns adjectives into adverbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示心智的拉丁名词、一个拉丁关系后缀，以及一个把形容词变成副词的英语后缀拼成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: a strong alcoholic drink made by distillation, alcoholic drink in general, or a liquid used in cooking or in an industrial process
core_image: 高脚杯里琥珀色的酒液轻轻一晃，杯壁上挂着一层薄光
scene: 深夜的柜子里只剩半瓶琥珀色的酒，主人把它倒进小杯。 He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 liquor 是「烈酒」（第 1 个义项：蒸馏得到的烈性酒）；句意为他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。图中可辨识物件：暗色酒柜、琥珀色酒液、炉火。

derivatives.zh: 由 liquor 加 -ous 构成，义为「酒味浓的；烈性的」，现代多用 alcoholic 替代
由 liquor 与 store 复合，义为「酒类专卖店」，主要用于北美
由 liquor 与 licence 复合，义为「酒类经营许可证」

senses.title: A strong distilled alcoholic drink
senses.definition: a strong alcoholic drink produced by distilling grain, fruit or other material
senses.definitionCN: 用谷物、水果等原料蒸馏而成的烈性酒
senses.example: He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。
senses.why: Latin liquor simply meant fluid, and early English used it for any liquid; distillation produced the strongest drinkable fluid, so the word settled on spirits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liquor 本只是「液体」，早期英语也用它指任何液体；蒸馏造出了最强烈的可饮液体，于是这个词落在了烈酒上。

senses.title: Alcoholic drink in general
senses.definition: alcoholic drink of any kind, as the word is used in laws and shops
senses.definitionCN: 任何种类的含酒精饮料，常见于法律与商店用语
senses.example: The state controls where liquor may be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个州管制烈酒可以在哪些地方出售。
senses.why: A law has to name the whole category it regulates, so the old word for fluid became the legal label for every drink containing alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 法律必须给它管制的整个类别起个名字，于是那个表示液体的旧词成了所有含酒精饮料的法律标签。

senses.title: The liquid left after cooking
senses.definition: the liquid left in the pot after food has been boiled or stewed
senses.definitionCN: 食物煮或炖之后留在锅里的液体
senses.example: She spooned the pot liquor over the greens.
senses.exampleCN: 她把锅里的汤汁舀到青菜上。
senses.why: Cooks saw the same thing chemists did, a flavoured fluid separated from solid food, and the old general sense of fluid made the name natural.
senses.whyCN: 厨子和化学家看到的是同一件事：从固体食物里分出来的一种有味液体；而 fluid 那个旧义让这个叫法显得再自然不过。

senses.title: A liquid in an industrial process
senses.definition: a liquid used or produced in an industrial or chemical process, such as the mother liquor left after crystals form
senses.definitionCN: 工业或化学过程中使用或产生的液体，如结晶后留下的母液
senses.example: The factory recycles the spent liquor instead of dumping it.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂回收用过的溶液，而不是把它倒掉。
senses.why: Industry needed a plain word for whatever flows through pipes and tanks, and it chose the Latin word for fluid rather than inventing a new term.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要一个朴素的词来指在管道和槽罐里流动的东西，于是选了拉丁语中「液体」那个词，而没有另造新术语。

intro.en: Liquor is a Latin noun for fluid that passed through French and narrowed in English from any liquid to strong drink.
intro.cn: liquor 是拉丁语中表示「液体」的名词，经法语传入英语后，从泛指液体缩小到专指烈酒。

items.en: Liquor was a Latin noun for fluid or liquid, formed from the verb that meant to be liquid.
items.cn: liquor 是拉丁语中表示「液体」的名词，由意为「呈液态」的动词构成。

items.en: The verb liquere meant to be fluid or clear, and it also gave liquidus, the adjective for something flowing.
items.cn: 动词 liquere 意为呈液态、清澈，它还给出了形容词 liquidus，用来描述流动的东西。

items.en: Old French took the word as licor or liquor, naming any liquid and later a drink.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 licor 或 liquor，泛指任何液体，后来也指饮品。

items.en: Middle English liquor could still mean any fluid, not only something to drink.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liquor 仍可指任何液体，而不只是能喝的东西。

items.en: Modern English narrows the everyday sense to strong drink, while chemistry keeps liquor for any liquid in a process.
items.cn: 现代英语把日常义项缩小到烈酒，而化学仍用 liquor 指工艺过程中的任何液体。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of flowing and being liquid; the near-meaning group gathers words for alcohol and strong drink.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「流动、呈液态」的词干展开；近义组收表示酒精与烈酒的词。

entries.definition: A substance that flows and is not solid.
entries.definitionCN: 液体；与 liquor 同出拉丁语 liquere。

entries.definition: To turn something into a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 使液化；由同一拉丁词干加 -fy 构成。

entries.definition: A sweet alcoholic drink served after a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 餐后甜酒；与 liquor 同出拉丁语 liquor，但经法语单独借入。

entries.definition: A sweet root used in sweets and medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 甘草；拼写与 liquor 相近，但词源来自希腊语，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The chemical in drinks that makes people drunk, or drink in general.
entries.definitionCN: 酒精；也泛指含酒精饮料。

entries.definition: Strong distilled alcoholic drinks.
A strong alcoholic drink distilled from wine.
entries.definitionCN: 白兰地；由葡萄酒蒸馏而成的烈酒。

entries.definition: Alcohol, especially in large amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 酒；口语说法，常指大量饮酒。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a Latin name for anything fluid, and its family keeps returning to flow, clarity and the strongest drink.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是拉丁语中泛指液体的名字，它的同族词反复回到流动、清澈以及最烈的酒。

normal.en: Latin liquor is simply fluid, and the word entered English as a general name for anything that flows.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 liquor 就是「液体」，这个词进入英语时是泛指一切流动之物的名字。

normal.en: The Latin verb liquere means to be liquid or clear, and it also gave the adjective liquidus.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 liquere 意为呈液态、清澈，它还给出了形容词 liquidus。

normal.en: Old French kept the word as licor for any liquid, and English narrowed the everyday sense to drink.
normal.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 licor，泛指任何液体；英语把日常义项缩小到了饮品。

normal.en: Distillation concentrates alcohol into the strongest fluid a still can produce, so liquor came to mean spirits.
normal.cn: 蒸馏把酒精浓缩成蒸馏器能造出的最强烈液体，于是 liquor 逐渐指烈酒。

normal.en: Mother liquor is the liquid left around crystals, so the same word still serves chemistry and the bar.
normal.cn: 母液是结晶之后留在晶体周围的液体，所以同一个词至今同时服务于化学实验室和酒吧。

abstract.en: A fluid takes the shape of whatever holds it, which is why liquor can name a drink, a bath and a broth without strain.
abstract.cn: 液体随容器改变形状，所以 liquor 能毫不费力地指一杯酒、一槽液体或一锅汤汁。

abstract.en: Alcohol is a liquid that burns, and the word carries both the cool flow and the hidden heat.
abstract.cn: 酒精是一种会燃烧的液体，这个词同时装着流动的凉意和藏起来的热。

abstract.en: Every language needs a plain word for what pours, and liquor is English's oldest answer.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都需要一个朴素的词来指会倾倒的东西，liquor 就是英语最老的答案。

examples.en: He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
examples.cn: 他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。

examples.en: The state controls where liquor may be sold.
examples.cn: 这个州管制烈酒可以在哪些地方出售。

examples.en: The factory recycles the spent liquor instead of dumping it.
examples.cn: 这家工厂回收用过的溶液，而不是把它倒掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立刻」——烈酒一入口，人立刻就上了头；liquor 是烈酒，也是会流动的液体。

root: 拉丁语 liquor（液体）来自动词 liquere（呈液态、清澈），经古法语 licur 进入英语；同族词多与流动、液体、清澈有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clear flowing fluid; from it come the distilled drink, the legal category of alcohol, the cooking broth and the industrial bath.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种清澈流动的液体；由此分出蒸馏酒、法律上的酒类、锅里的汤汁，以及工业用的溶液。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: amber liquid swaying in a glass, leaving a thin film of light on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：琥珀色的酒液在杯中晃动，在杯壁上留下一层薄薄的光。

branches.en: a bottle of amber spirit standing in a dark cabinet
branches.cn: 暗柜里一瓶琥珀色的烈酒

branches.en: a shop window stacked with labelled bottles
branches.cn: 橱窗里摆满贴标签的酒瓶

branches.en: a spoon lifting broth from a pot
branches.cn: 勺子从锅里舀起汤汁

branches.en: a tank of cloudy liquid in a factory
branches.cn: 工厂里一罐浑浊的液体

branches.en: a licence pinned beside the till
branches.cn: 收银台旁钉着的许可证

intro.en: A Latin noun for fluid, its verb and adjective, one French reshaping and two English suffixes carry liquor from running water to strong drink and chemical baths.
intro.cn: 一个表示液体的拉丁名词、它的动词与形容词、一次法语改写，再加两个英语后缀，把 liquor 从流动的水带到烈酒与化学溶液。

latinIntro.en: Liquor, liquere and liquidus are all recorded Latin words built on the same stem for flowing and being clear.
latinIntro.cn: liquor、liquere 与 liquidus 都是有记录的拉丁词，建立在同一个表示「流动、清澈」的词干上。

items.meaning: to be liquid, to be clear

latinEntries.meaning: to be liquid, to be clear

definition_zh: 古董；古物；古老的；古董的
definition_en: an object from an earlier period valued for its age, or an adjective describing such objects
core_image: 旧货店里落着薄尘的黄铜座钟
scene: 街角的小店摆满旧家具，铜器泛着暗光。 She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
sceneCN: 这里 antique 是「古董的」（第 2 个义项：形容年代久远且有价值的物品）；句意是她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

derivatives.zh: 名词：古代；古物，同源于拉丁语 antiquus
形容词：研究古物（收藏）的

senses.title: An object from the past
senses.definition: a piece of furniture, jewellery, or other object that is old and valued for its age
senses.definitionCN: 年代久远、因年代而受珍视的家具、首饰或其他物件
senses.example: She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
senses.exampleCN: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。
senses.why: Latin antiquus meant 'former, ancient', and the noun use in English picked out objects that survive from that former time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antiquus 意为「从前的、古老的」，英语里的名词用法挑出的就是从那个从前留存下来的物件。

senses.title: Belonging to an earlier period
senses.definition: used of furniture, objects, or styles that come from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 用于来自较早时代的家具、物件或样式
senses.example: The room was full of antique furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里摆满了古董家具。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain temporal meaning of antiquus, so anything surviving from an earlier age can be called antique.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了 antiquus 单纯的时间含义，因此任何从较早年代留存下来的东西都能叫 antique。

senses.title: Old-fashioned, out of date
senses.definition: used in a slightly mocking way for ideas or methods that belong to the past
senses.definitionCN: 略带嘲意地指属于过去的思想或方法
senses.example: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。
senses.why: Once a thing is old enough to be quaint, the same word can belittle an idea as a museum piece.
senses.whyCN: 当一样东西旧到显得古怪时，同一个词也能把某种观念贬为博物馆里的陈列品。

intro.en: Antique descends from a Latin word for 'former' built on ante, 'before'.
intro.cn: antique 来自拉丁语中表示「从前的」的词，词根是 ante「在前」。

items.en: ante meant 'before' and remains in words such as anterior.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」，仍见于 anterior 等词。

items.en: antiquus meant 'old, former, of long ago'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「旧的、从前的、很久以前的」。

items.en: Old French antique passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 antique 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English first used antique of ancient times and old remains.
items.cn: 英语 antique 最初用于古代与古代遗存。

items.en: By the nineteenth century antique had narrowed to valued old objects and their style.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，antique 已收窄为指受珍视的旧物及其风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for old; the near-meaning group is other words for things from the past.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「旧」的拉丁词根；近义组是其他指旧物的词。

entries.definition: the ancient past, or an object from it
old and no longer useful
being the only one of its kind
entries.definitionCN: 独特的；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: old but of good quality, especially clothing or wine
an object surviving from the past
an object valued by collectors

normalIntro.en: Antique means old enough to be kept and valued.
normalIntro.cn: antique 就是旧到值得被收藏珍视。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable: an-TIQUE.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：an-TIQUE。

normal.en: An antique is a thing; antique as an adjective describes it.
normal.cn: antique 作名词指物件，作形容词则表示「古董的」。

normal.en: Antique shop and antique furniture are the two most common pairs.
normal.cn: antique shop 与 antique furniture 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Antiquity is the abstract noun; antique is the object.
normal.cn: antiquity 是抽象名词，antique 指具体物件。

normal.en: Do not spell it antic; the que comes from French.
normal.cn: 不要写成 antic，词尾 que 来自法语。

abstract.en: See dust on a brass clock face.
abstract.cn: 想象黄铜钟面上的一层薄尘。

abstract.en: See a price tag tied with old string.
abstract.cn: 想象用旧绳系着的价签。

abstract.en: See a modern chair beside a carved wooden one.
abstract.cn: 想象现代椅子旁边那把雕花木椅。

examples.en: She found a brass clock in an antique shop.
examples.cn: 她在古董店找到一只黄铜钟。

examples.en: The room was full of antique furniture.
examples.cn: 房间里摆满了古董家具。

examples.en: His antique views on marriage surprised the class.
examples.cn: 他对婚姻的陈旧看法让全班很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: anti（前）加 -que：从前留下来的东西，就是古董。

root: 来自拉丁语 antiquus「古代的、从前的」，由 ante「在前」加词尾构成，经古法语 antique 进入英语；同根词有 antiquity、antiquated、antiquarian。

sensesIntro.en: The same age-word names an old object, describes an old style, and mocks an outdated idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「旧」词既能指旧物，也能形容旧样式，还能嘲讽过时的观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass clock that has outlived its first owners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只比最初主人活得更久的黄铜钟。

branches.en: a shop full of antiques
branches.cn: 摆满古董的店铺

branches.en: a genuine antique
branches.cn: 一件真古董

branches.en: antique furniture
branches.cn: 古董家具

branches.en: antique lace
branches.cn: 古董蕾丝

branches.en: antique ideas
branches.cn: 陈旧的观念

intro.en: A Latin adjective of age that English uses as both noun and adjective.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示年代的拉丁语形容词，英语中兼作名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root antiquus also gives antiquity and antiquated.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 antiquus 也派生出 antiquity 与 antiquated。

items.meaning: old but fine, as of wine

definition_zh: 假想的；想象中的；虚构的
definition_en: existing only in the mind and not in the real world
core_image: 孩子给空椅子端上一杯茶，认真地和看不见的客人说话
scene: 午后的客厅里只有她一个人。 Her imaginary friend sat on the blue chair, so she poured two cups and chatted to the empty seat.
sceneCN: 这里 imaginary 是「想象中的、虚构的」（第 1 个义项：只存在于头脑中），句意是她想象中的朋友坐在蓝椅子上，于是她倒了两杯茶对着空座位说话。画面里有午后的客厅和那只空椅子。

pos.zh: 形容词：假想的、想象中的、虚构的

senses.title: Existing only in the mind
senses.definition: created by the mind and having no physical reality
senses.definitionCN: 由头脑创造、并无实体存在的
senses.example: The child blamed the mess on an imaginary friend.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子把弄乱的东西推给一个想象出来的朋友。
senses.why: The -ary ending marks a quality, so the word describes things that live only inside the imagination.
senses.whyCN: -ary 词尾标示一种性质，这个词因此形容只活在想象里的事物。

senses.title: Not real in a practical sense
senses.definition: invented rather than based on fact, often used of fears or problems
senses.definitionCN: 凭空造出而非依据事实的，多用于恐惧或问题
senses.example: His worries about the interview turned out to be imaginary.
senses.exampleCN: 他关于面试的担忧后来证明是自寻烦恼。
senses.why: When something invented keeps a person anxious, English calls the worry itself imaginary rather than calling the person dishonest.
senses.whyCN: 当虚构之物让人焦灼时，英语称这份忧虑为 imaginary，而不指责人撒谎。

senses.title: A line drawn only for convenience
senses.definition: used of lines or points drawn to explain geometry or geography, though nothing visible is there
senses.definitionCN: 用于几何或地理中便于说明而设想出的线或点
senses.example: The equator is an imaginary line around the earth's middle.
senses.exampleCN: 赤道是环绕地球中部的一条假想线。
senses.why: Science often needs a line nobody can see, and the word labels such tools without doubting their usefulness.
senses.whyCN: 科学常需要一条谁也看不见的线，这个词标出这类工具，却并不否定它们的用处。

intro.en: Imaginary is built on the same Latin root as image, with an ending that turns a likeness into a quality.
intro.cn: imaginary 与 image 同出拉丁词根，词尾把这层「形貌」转成一种性质。

items.en: Imago meant a likeness, and imaginarius described what existed only as a likeness in the mind.
items.cn: 拉丁语 imago 指形貌，imaginarius 则形容只以心中影像而存在的东西。

items.en: Latin writers already used imaginarius of dreams, shadows and empty fears.
items.cn: 拉丁作家已用 imaginarius 形容梦、影子与凭空而来的恐惧。

items.en: French kept imaginari, and medieval schoolmen debated whether such things could be said to exist.
items.cn: 法语保留 imaginari 形式，中世纪学者争论这类事物能否算作存在。

items.en: English adopted it as imaginary in the fourteenth century, mostly in religious and philosophical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 imaginary 借入，多用于宗教与哲学文本。

items.en: Children's stories and psychology made imaginary a plain everyday word, often before the noun friend.
items.cn: 儿童文学与心理学让 imaginary 成为平常词，常放在 friend 之前。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for what is not real.
note.cn: 形近组收同词根的形容词；近义组收表示「不真实」的词。

entries.definition: Full of new ideas; not false, but inventive.
entries.definitionCN: 富有创意的，并非虚假而是有新意。

entries.definition: Possible to picture in the mind.
Relating to an image or to the imagination, a rarer relative.
entries.definitionCN: 与影像或想象有关的，较少见。

entries.definition: Invented for a story, openly not real.
entries.definitionCN: 为故事虚构的，公开承认不真。

entries.definition: Not existing in fact, or seeming too strange to be true.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上不存在的，或奇异得不像真的。

entries.definition: Real but unable to be seen; a frequent confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 真实却看不见，常被误与 imaginary 混用。

normalIntro.en: The hooks separate imaginary from imaginative and tie it to empty chairs and drawn lines.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 imaginary 与 imaginative 区分开，并把它系到空椅子和画出来的线上。

normal.en: If -ary is there, the thing is not real; if -ive appears, the thing is creative.
normal.cn: 有 -ary 就不真实；换成 -ive 就表示有创造力。

normal.en: The ending -ary is the one in dictionary: a place where words are, not where things are.
normal.cn: -ary 正是 dictionary 的词尾：一册收录词的地方，不是实物的所在地。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable from the end: im-AG-i-na-ry.
normal.cn: 重音在倒数第三音节：im-AG-i-na-ry。

normal.en: An imaginary friend can be loved and fed, but no chair beneath is warm.
normal.cn: 想象中的朋友可以被爱、被喂，但座位底下没有一丝温度。

normal.en: The equator is imaginary too, yet ships rely on it daily.
normal.cn: 赤道也是假想的，可船只每天都要靠它。

abstract.en: The word does not mock the mind; it simply marks the border where a picture stops having weight.
abstract.cn: 这个词并不嘲笑头脑，它只标出那幅画失去重量的边界。

abstract.en: Things that exist only in the mind can still frighten us, which is why the word often follows the noun fear.
abstract.cn: 只存在于头脑的东西也能吓人，所以这个词常跟在「恐惧」之后。

abstract.en: Every map is partly imaginary, and that is exactly what makes it usable.
abstract.cn: 每张地图都带几分假想，而这恰是它可用的原因。

examples.en: As a boy he had an imaginary horse in the garden.
examples.cn: 小时候他在花园里养着一匹想象出来的马。

examples.en: The border is an imaginary line drawn on a map.
examples.cn: 这条边界是地图上画的一条假想线。

examples.en: Most of his fears were imaginary, not medical.
examples.cn: 他的恐惧大多是想象出来的，并非医学问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: imagin 想象 + ary 形容词尾——只存在于想象里的，即假想的

root: 拉丁语 imago（词干 imagin-）「形貌」加形容词词尾 -arius，经古法语 imaginari 进入英语，十四世纪定形 imaginary。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: existing only in the mind, invented rather than factual, and drawn for convenience.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：只存在于头脑、虚构而非事实，以及为方便而设定的假想线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child pouring tea for an empty blue chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子对着空着的蓝椅子倒茶。

branches.en: THE PLAY LINE: imaginary friends and games belong to childhood.
branches.cn: 游戏线：想象中的朋友与游戏属于童年。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: imaginary worries are invented and can be dismissed.
branches.cn: 心事线：想象出来的担忧是凭空造的，也能被放下。

branches.en: THE MAP LINE: the equator and borders are imaginary but useful.
branches.cn: 地图线：赤道与国界是假想的，却很有用。

branches.en: THE BORDER LINE: nothing in these senses can be touched.
branches.cn: 边界线：这几种用法里的事物都摸不到。

branches.en: THE MIND LINE: in both, the mind supplies what the world does not.
branches.cn: 头脑线：两种情况下，都是头脑补上了世界没给的东西。

intro.en: Imaginary pairs the image root with the adjective ending -ary, and its cousins make the contrast clear.
intro.cn: imaginary 把 image 的词根与形容词词尾 -ary 配在一起，几个同族词正好显出对比。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective imaginarius is recorded, so the English word is a direct descendant, not a new coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 imaginarius 有文献记录，英语此词是直接继承，而非新造。

items.example: Ordinary and military use it too.
items.exampleCN: ordinary 与 military 也用这一词尾。
一个富有想象力的方案奏效了。
最难以想象的暴风雨来了。

items.example: The image faded on the screen.
items.exampleCN: 屏幕上的影像渐渐淡去。

definition_en: the quality of being correct or exact
core_image: 一支箭正落在靶心的十字交点上
scene: 天气预报说准了下雨的时间，农民都很惊讶。 The accuracy of the forecast surprised the farmers.
sceneCN: 这里的 accuracy 是「与事实相符的准确」（第 1 个义项：信息正确）；句意是预报之准让农民吃惊。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀构成形容词，义为「准确的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「准确地」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确；误差」
加否定前缀构成，义为「不准确的」

senses.title: Fidelity to the facts
senses.definition: the quality of being correct and true in matters of fact
senses.definitionCN: 在事实层面正确、无误的性质
senses.example: Nobody doubted the accuracy of her report.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人怀疑她报告的准确性。
senses.why: The Latin root cura means care, so accuracy first names the care that keeps a statement from drifting away from the truth.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cura 意为「用心」，所以 accuracy 最初指的是那份让陈述不偏离事实的用心。

senses.title: Closeness of a measurement
senses.definition: the degree to which a measurement or calculation matches the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计算结果与真实值接近的程度
senses.example: The accuracy of the scale was tested with known weights.
senses.exampleCN: 人们用已知重量的砝码检测这台秤的精度。
senses.why: An instrument shows its care by repeating the same true value; the noun moves from honest speech to calibrated metal.
senses.whyCN: 仪器靠反复给出同一个真实值来体现「用心」，这个词于是从说实话挪到了校准过的金属上。

senses.title: Steadiness in hitting a target
senses.definition: the ability to send a shot or throw to the intended point
senses.definitionCN: 把射击或投掷送到预定点的能力
senses.example: Her accuracy with a bow improved after months of practice.
senses.exampleCN: 练了几个月后，她的射箭准头提高了。
senses.why: Here the true value is a point on a target, and care becomes the steady hand that repeats the same aim.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「真实值」是靶上的一个点，而「用心」变成了那只每次都瞄准同一点、稳稳不放的手。

intro.en: The word grows from Latin care, not from a root meaning sharp or fast.
intro.cn: 这个词长自拉丁语的「用心」，而不是表示锋利或快速的字根。

items.en: cura meant care, attention or trouble taken over something.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、留意，或为某事费的心。

items.en: accuratus described something done with care and therefore exact.
items.cn: accuratus 形容某事做得用心，因而精确。

items.en: the noun accuratio named careful exactness.
items.cn: 名词 accuratio 指用心的精确。

items.en: accuracy entered English as a noun of exactness in statement and measure.
items.cn: accuracy 在十七世纪进入英语，指陈述与度量上的精确。

items.en: it now covers news reports, laboratory data and rifle scores.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖新闻报道、实验室数据与射击成绩。

note.en: The first group is the accurate family; the second is other words for exactness.
note.cn: 第一组是 accurate 词族；第二组是别的表示精确的说法。

entries.definition: correct in every detail
in a correct and exact way
a lack of correctness
not correct or exact
the quality of being exact and repeatable
strict correctness in every detail
freedom from error
closeness to an original or a fact

normalIntro.en: The key is Latin cura, care, which also lives in cure and curator.
normalIntro.cn: 关键是拉丁语 cura（用心），cure、curator 里也有它。

normal.en: cura means care, so accuracy is the fruit of taking care.
normal.cn: cura 意为用心，accuracy 就是用心的果实。

normal.en: the adjective accurate drops the noun ending and keeps the stem.
normal.cn: 形容词 accurate 去掉名词词尾，保留同一个词干。

normal.en: in- before accuracy reverses it into error.
normal.cn: 在 accuracy 前加 in- 就翻成误差。

normal.en: measurement accuracy and accuracy rate are the usual technical pairs.
normal.cn: measurement accuracy 与 accuracy rate 是常见的技术搭配。

normal.en: pinpoint accuracy is the phrase for an almost perfect hit.
normal.cn: pinpoint accuracy 形容几乎分毫不差的命中。

abstract.en: See an arrow settle exactly in the centre of the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭不偏不倚扎进靶心。

abstract.en: Picture a scale needle stopping on the true weight.
abstract.cn: 想象秤的指针停在真实重量上。

abstract.en: Think of a reporter checking every name twice before printing.
abstract.cn: 想象记者发稿前把每个人名核了两遍。

examples.en: The accuracy of the map saved the hikers from a wrong turn.
examples.cn: 地图的准确让徒步者免于走错路。

examples.en: Modern instruments measure temperature with great accuracy.
examples.cn: 现代仪器能非常精确地测量温度。

examples.en: His accuracy at the dartboard impressed the whole pub.
examples.cn: 他在飞镖盘前的准头让整个酒馆都佩服。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克尤乐西」——阿克每次投镖都先瞄准半天，投出去正中西边靶心。

root: 拉丁语 accuratus（用心的、精确的），源自 ad-（朝向）与 cura（关心、留意）；本义是「用心做」，引申为与事实或真值相符。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of care branches into honest words, calibrated instruments and steady aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「用心」分作三支：诚实的话、校准的仪器、稳定的瞄准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark that lands exactly where it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：落在应落之处的那个点。

branches.en: a report that matches what really happened
branches.cn: 与实际发生之事相符的报道

branches.en: an instrument that returns the true value
branches.cn: 给出真实值的仪器

branches.en: a hand that sends the shot to the mark
branches.cn: 把箭送到靶点的那只手

branches.en: care shown both in speech and in action
branches.cn: 说话与动作里同样体现的用心

branches.en: numbers you can trust because someone checked them
branches.cn: 因为有人核对过而可信的数字

intro.en: A Latin care-root, a participle ending and a noun suffix build the word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「用心」的拉丁词根、一个分词词尾和一个名词后缀，构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: cura, care, also gives cure, curator and curious through related Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: cura（用心）经由相关拉丁形式也给出 cure、curator 与 curious。
